SUBJECT:  APPROVE DOWN-PAYMENT ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Down-Payment Assistance Program; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager Pro Tem or his designee to execute any documents
  related to the implementation of the Down-Payment Assistance Program and to
  review and approve non-substantial revisions to the program.

BACKGROUND

The City Council approved the five-year plan (The Plan) for the State of California
Department of Housing and Community Development’s (HCD) Permanent Local
Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program on July 14, 2020. The PLHA funding is generated
from the Building Homes and Jobs Act, SB2, which established a $75 recording fee on
real estate documents to increase the supply of affordable housing in California. The
Plan includes providing down-payment assistance to those trying to purchase their first
home.

DISCUSSION

The Down-Payment Assistance Program (Program) has been designed to assist families
and individuals who wish to purchase their first home but cannot secure a sufficient down
payment or pay closing costs.

The Program offers a limited number of deferred-payment second trust deed loans. It is
designed to provide qualified households with down payment and closing cost assistance
when purchasing a single-family home (detached or attached), condominium, or
townhome in the City of Palmdale.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Down-Payment Assistance Program
April 15, 2025
Page 2

This Program aims to offset some of the impact of high housing costs on households
while encouraging investment in the community. The Program will assist households
whose incomes are up to 150% of the Area Median Income (AMI) by providing down
payment and closing cost assistance for up to 49% of the purchase price, not to exceed
$200,000 based on need.

Potential homebuyers must not have had an ownership interest in a principal residence
at any time within the past three (3) years; are required to provide a minimum of 3% of
the purchase price as their portion of the down payment; must complete an approved in-
person Homebuyer Education course; and must execute all documents related to the City
loan including Affordable Housing Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions.

The provision of assistance, in accordance with the Program, promotes owner-occupied
homeownership and provides an investment in our community.

FISCAL IMPACT

$410,100; Funds are budgeted in Down-Payment Assistance account. Additional funding
may be identified through the budget process.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal IV: Maintain a desirable community where everyone wants to live, work and play.

  D. Develop and maintain diverse programs and events that inspire growth, pride,
  and lifelong learning.

Atch 1 Down-Payment Assistance Program Overview
   CITY OF PALMDALE
  DOWN-PAYMENT ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

  OVERVIEW

PROGRAM DESCRIPTION:

The Program offers down payment and closing cost assistance with a limited number of
zero-interest, deferred-payment second trust deed loans. It is specifically designed to
provide qualified households with down-payment and closing costs assistance when
purchasing a house in the City of Palmdale.

The Program has been designed to assist families and individuals who wish to purchase
a home but cannot secure a sufficient down payment or afford high closing costs to qualify
for an affordable loan. This Program intends to offset some of the impact of high housing
costs on households while encouraging investment in the community. A Program loan
provides down payment and closing cost assistance as a silent second mortgage to
eligible first-time purchasers in the City of Palmdale. To qualify as a first-time home buyer,
the Participant cannot have held an ownership interest in any property for the last 3 years.

Participants will be pre-screened for participation in the Program based on a basic
eligibility questionnaire. Once screened, the Participant will submit a full application. The
Participant will work with a primary lender and real estate agent to establish primary
mortgage funding and locate a residence within the City. The participant will be required
to complete an 8-hour Homebuyer Education Program Seminar before the close of
escrow.

The Participant must contribute no less than 3% of the purchase price of the home as
their portion of the down payment. The primary lender must provide a fully amortized, 30-
year fixed-rate mortgage. No adjustable-rate mortgages are acceptable under this
Program. The City will provide a zero-interest 30-year deferred second mortgage. The
combination of the Participant's down payment and the primary and secondary mortgage
allows for an affordable monthly housing cost. The Participant must occupy the residence
as their primary residence for the term of the Program loan.

The Program also requires the execution of a Loan Agreement, Promissory Note, Second
Deed of Trust, and Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (C,C & R’s), which include
the terms on the transfer of the property before the full term of the Program loan.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2025-025, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE DIRECTING THE
  PREPARATION OF THE ANNUAL ENGINEER’S REPORT FOR THE
  CONTINUATION OF THE ANNUAL LEVY OF ASSESSMENTS AND
  DESIGNATING THE ENGINEER OF WORK FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2025-26 FOR THE CITY OF PALMDALE DRAINAGE BENEFIT
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICTS NO. 1, AND NO. 2006-02

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2025-025, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale directing the preparation of the annual Engineer’s Report for the
  continuation of the annual levy of assessments and designating the Engineer of
  Work fiscal year 2025-26 for the City of Palmdale Drainage Benefit Assessment
  Districts No. 1, and No. 2006-02; and,

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute Resolution No. CC 2025-025, directing the
  preparation of the annual Engineer’s Report for the continuation of the annual
  levy of assessments and designating the Engineer of Work for the City of
  Palmdale Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts No. 1, and No. 2006-02.

BACKGROUND

During the entitlement review of the Anaverde and Ritter Ranch developments, it was
determined that the formations of drainage benefit assessment districts were necessary
to fund the maintenance of drainage facilities for each of these Master Planned
Communities. As a result, the formations of the Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts
No. 1 (Anaverde), and No. 2006-02 (Ritter Ranch) were approved by the property
owners on May 12, 2004, and January 3, 2007, respectively, pursuant to mailed ballot
elections conducted in accordance with Article XIIID of the California Constitution.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Reso. No. CC 2025-025
April 15, 2025
Page 2

The purpose of the Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts is to fund the installation,
construction, or maintenance of any authorized improvements under the Benefit
Assessment Act of 1982 (California Government Code Section 54703 et seq.). These
improvements include but are not limited to drainage improvements and any facilities
appurtenant to those improvements or necessary or convenient for their maintenance
and servicing.

DISCUSSION

Resolution No. CC 2025-025 designates NBS as the Engineer of Work and directs the
preparation of the annual Engineer’s Report for Fiscal Year 2025-26 for the City of
Palmdale Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts No. 1, and No. 2006-02.

Each year, for the City to continue to levy annual assessments within the Drainage
Benefit Assessment Districts, the City must have a detailed Engineer’s Report approved
by the City Council. The attached resolution, ordering the preparation of the combined
annual Engineer’s Report, initiates the proceedings for the annual levy of assessments
for the Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts No. 1, and No. 2006-02 for Fiscal Year
2025-26.

The annual Engineer’s Report will be presented to the City Council at the June 3, 2025,
meeting. A public hearing will be held on July 1, 2025, at the City Council meeting to
accept public testimony regarding the annual report and authorize the levy of
assessments for Fiscal Year 2025-26.

FISCAL IMPACT

Levy amounts will be included with the Engineer’s Report to be presented at the June
3, 2025, City Council meeting.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.

  A. Manage resources, costs and liabilities to ensure the City's long-term fiscal
  health.

  B. Establish healthy reserves for ongoing replacement and repair of capital
  while stabilizing annual spending.

April 15, 2025

  levy of assessments and designating the engineer of work for fiscal year 2025-

  Streetlight Maintenance Assessment Districts and Annexations.

April 15, 2025
Page 2

BACKGROUND

The City’s Landscape Maintenance Assessment Districts and Annexations, Park
Maintenance, and Recreation Improvement District, and Streetlight Maintenance
Assessment Districts and Annexations (all together referred to as the “Districts”) were
approved by property owners pursuant to mailed ballot elections conducted in
accordance with Article XIIID of the California Constitution and the Landscaping and
Lighting Act of 1972 (the "Act"), Part 2 of Division 15 of the California Streets and
Highways Code (commencing with Section 22500 thereof).

The purpose of the Landscape Maintenance Assessment Districts and Annexations is
to fund the installation, maintenance, and servicing of ornamental structures,
landscaping, including trees, shrubs, grass and other ornamental vegetation, and
appurtenant facilities, including irrigation systems, drainage devices, and dry wells
located in public places within the boundaries of the Landscape Maintenance
Assessment Districts and Annexations.

The purpose of the Park Maintenance and Recreation Improvement District is to fund
the installation, maintenance, and servicing of public parks and recreational facilities
throughout the City.

The purpose of the Streetlight Maintenance Assessment Districts and Annexations is to
fund the installation, maintenance, and servicing of any authorized improvements under
the Act, including, but not limited to, streetlights, traffic signals, and highway safety light
improvements, and any facilities which are appurtenant to any of those mentioned above
or which are necessary or convenient for the maintenance or servicing thereof.

DISCUSSION

Resolution No. CC 2025-026 designates NBS as the Engineer of Work and directs the
preparation of the annual Engineer’s Reports for Fiscal Year 2025-26 for each of these
City Districts.

The Landscaping and Lighting Act of 1972 requires that the districts have a detailed
engineer’s report approved by the city council each year to continue the annual
assessment levy. The attached resolution, ordering the preparation of the annual
Engineer’s Reports, initiates the proceedings for the annual assessment levy for the
Districts for Fiscal Year 2025-26.

The annual Engineer’s Reports will be presented to the City Council at the June 3, 2025,
meeting. A public hearing will be held on July 1, 2025, at the City Council meeting to
accept public testimony regarding the combined annual Engineer’s Report and levy of
assessments for Fiscal Year 2025-26.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt of Reso. No. CC 2025-026
April 15, 2025
Page 3

FISCAL IMPACT

Levy amounts will be included with the combined annual Engineer’s Reports presented
at the June 3, 2025, City Council meeting.

  A. Manage resources, costs and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

  B. Establish healthy reserves for ongoing replacement and repair of capital
  while stabilizing annual spending.

BACKGROUND

The County Sanitation District No. 14 of Los Angeles County has requested that the City
enter into a tax-sharing agreement for parcel numbers 3005-010-025 and 3005-010-026
as shown in the attached Annexation No. 464 Map. These parcels are part of a proposed
new gas station and drive-through restaurant located on the southwest corner of 10th
Street West and Avenue O. This annexation is a condition of the development’s
entitlement and is required before it can receive sewer service.

Under the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01), any time there is a
jurisdictional change that results in a special district providing a new service not
previously provided to an area, the law requires the governing bodies of all local
agencies that receive a portion of that property tax determine by resolution the amount
of the annual tax increase to be transferred to that special district. The existing ad
velorem tax revenue based on the property’s assessed value received by agencies will
not change. This action only affects that portion of future tax revenues based on
increases in assessed property value.

DISCUSSION

Adoption of this Resolution will be in accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code
between public agencies currently receiving tax revenue from these parcels and the
County Sanitation District No. 14. Through the referenced annexation, the Sanitation
District will be providing off-site sewage disposal services to this parcel for the first time.
All the referenced agencies and special districts will execute similar resolutions and are
parties to the proportional tax adjustment.

FISCAL IMPACT

The current property tax share ratio for the City of Palmdale within the area of this
annexation is 6.6247%. This Council action will allocate 0.0396% of any future tax
increase to County Sanitation District No. 14, resulting in a net tax share rate for the city
of 6.5851%. This allocation follows the State Revenue and Taxation Code, and the

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Third Amendment to Agreement No. A-8149 with SOV Security for PN
  872, Citywide Security Upgrades Project increasing the Agreement by $255,750,
  for the total not to exceed amount of $1,525,616, which includes an amendment
  amount of $204,600, plus a 25 % contingency of $51,150 with an extension of 180
  calendar days, with a completion date of October 12, 2025, and;

  2. Authorize the City Manager Pro Tem or his designee to execute the third
  Amendment to Agreement No. A-8149 with SOV Security, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

On April 5, 2023, the City Council awarded SOV Security a construction contract for
citywide security upgrades (Project) to City Hall, the Development Services Building,
the Palmdale Transportation Center, the Maintenance Yard, and the Palmdale
Playhouse in the amount of $973,833 for a term of 365 calendar days. The Project will
provide a fully integrated end-to-end physical security system with video surveillance
and access control functionality.

On August 3, 2023, Supplemental Agreement No. 1 was executed for $50,058.03 after
a project team site walk, assessment, and discussion of specific device locations, which
 Report to Mayor and City Council

Page 2

resulted in identifying additional needs, including mounting hardware, door
modifications, additional extra cameras, additional access control locations, and labor.

On August 28, 2024, a Second Amendment to Agreement No. A-8149 was executed for
$41,374.62 to add door strikes and Cisco switches at the Palmdale Transportation
Center, a front door release button for the City Hall main entry, and two camera poles
at the Maintenance Yard. With this amendment, 35 calendar days were added to the
Project for a total of 400 calendar days.

DISCUSSION

Additional security risk areas have been identified and must be addressed to complete a
fully comprehensive security system. This amendment includes additional access-
controlled doors for Human Resources, Palmdale Transportation Center, Development
Services, and City Hall, including a complete exterior camera system at the Palmdale City
Library.

These additional tasks require materials with lead times and labor for installations and
programming. A 25% contingency of $51,150 has been included to cover unforeseen
conditions and additional security improvements that may be identified during work.

Although Phase I of this project is nearly complete, staff and contractors continue to
identify areas potentially requiring the relocation of equipment, such as camera placement
and/or door access. Phase I includes multiple locations: City Hall, Development Services,
Maintenance Yard, the Playhouse, and the Palmdale Transportation Center. With this
amendment, 180 calendar days were added to the Project.

FISCAL IMPACT

$255,750; The Project is funded in Account No. F0083, Measure AV (157), and Prop A
Funds (203). Sufficient funds are budgeted and available in FY 2024-25.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Third Amendment to Agreement No. A-8161 with Schneider Electric for
  PN 880, ESCO Energy Project, for professional services, increasing the
  agreement by $84,450 for a total not to exceed amount of $15,336,605 with an
  extension of three months for a total term of 22 months; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager Pro Tem or his designee to execute the Third
  Amendment to Agreement No. A-8161 with Schneider Electric, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

In March 2023, the City Council awarded Schneider Electric a professional services
contract for $8,491,602 to provide design-build services for the installation of energy-
efficient replacements for outdated lighting, HVAC, and irrigation controls.

On November 11, 2023, the First Amendment was approved for $6,172,270, adding
interior and exterior LED lighting, sports field LED retrofit lighting, and HVAC TAB
reports to the scope of work.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Third Amendment to Agrmt No. A-8161
April 15, 2025
Page 2

On December 2, 2024, the Second Amendment was approved for $588,283, adding
smart irrigation to several City Parks and facilities and structural upgrades to City Hall
and the SAVES buildings to accommodate new HVAC units to the scope of work.

DISCUSSION

As part of this project, the HVAC units in the City Hall Administrative building were
replaced. With the replacements, deficiencies in the existing ducting became evident, and
a cold spot was identified in an area of the building. Due to this, duct dampers must be
installed to evenly distribute the heating and cooling in this area.

Additionally, in early 2024, the recently installed sports field lighting panel at Pelona Vista
Park was vandalized, causing the sports lighting to stop functioning. Schneider Electric
will replace the lighting controls and contactors, replace removed wiring from the
controller panel, and reprogram the system to restore functionality. Approval of this
Amendment will directly address these issues.

FISCAL IMPACT

$84,450; This project is funded using G0167157 and G0167158, Measure AV and the
General Fund. Sufficient funds are budgeted and available in FY 2024-25.

DATE:  APRIL 15, 2025

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT
  MAINTENANCE DIVISION

DISTRICT:  ALL

SUBJECT:  APPROVE REQUISITION WITH NATIONAL AUTO FLEET FOR THE
  PURCHASE OF TWO NEW ROADLINE GPMT GRAFFITI TRUCKS
  FOR A TOTAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF $334,500; AND
  APPROVE REQUISITION WITH INLAND KENWORTH (US), INC.,
  FOR THE PURCHASE OF A NEW T880 SUPER 10 DUMP TRUCK
  FOR A TOTAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF $285,000; AND
  APPROVE REQUISITION WITH MUNICIPAL MAINTENANCE
  EQUIPMENT FOR THE PURCHASE OF A NEW PETERSEN
  LIGHTNING LOADER FOR A TOTAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF
  $295,000; AND APPROVE REQUISITION WITH PB LOADER
  CORPORATION FOR THE PURCHASE OF A NEW B-5 ASPHALT
  TRUCK FOR A TOTAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF $360,000

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Requisition No. 250913 and resulting purchase order with National Auto
  Fleet, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes, for the purchase of two
  (2) new Roadline GPMT Graffiti Trucks for a total not to exceed amount of
  $334,500;

  2. Approve Requisition No. 250915 and resulting purchase order with Inland
  Kenworth (US), Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantial changes, for the
  purchase of a new T880 Super 10 Dump Truck for a total not to exceed amount of
  $285,000;

  3. Approve Requisition No. 250917 and resulting purchase order with Municipal
  Maintenance Equipment, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes, for
  the purchase of a new Petersen Lightning Loader for a total not to exceed amount
  of $295,000;
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Requisitions No. 250913 with National Auto Fleet, No. 250915 with Inland
Kenworth (US), Inc., No. 250917 with Municipal Maintenance Equipment, & No. 250930
with PB Loader Corporation
April 15, 2025
Page 2

  4. Approve Requisition No. 250930 and resulting purchase order with PB Loader
  Corporation, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes, for the purchase
  of a new B-5 Asphalt Truck for a total not to exceed amount of $360,000;

BACKGROUND

The City’s Fleet Maintenance Division manages over 350 vehicles, equipment, and
specialty equipment. It coordinates, develops, and recommends long-range plans for
managing and maintaining fleet operations, including purchasing vehicles under the
City’s Vehicle Replacement Policy and supporting departmental needs.

The Policy considers a vehicle’s age, miles or hours used, and duty type to determine
which vehicles and equipment are eligible and most in need of replacement. Based on
these criteria, staff identified the City’s current paving machine and two repurposed
graffiti service trucks for replacement. Additionally, two new vehicles, a dump truck and
a lightning loader, are needed to outfit approved operator positions.

The funds to purchase these new and replacement items were approved within the
original and mid-year budget adoption for Fiscal Year 2024-25.

DISCUSSION

The addition of these vehicles will improve efficiency and reduce equipment waiting
times, enhance service delivery for critical infrastructure operations and projects, reduce
reliance on costly long-term equipment rentals, allow for better resource allocation and
timely responses to maintenance needs, and ensure that critical tasks are completed
without delay, ultimately improving safety and satisfaction for residents and businesses.

Roadline Model GPMT Graffiti Removal Trucks

Graffiti continues to be one of the leading issues faced in our community. While the City
has made significant strides in swiftly removing vandalism from public spaces and
maintaining a cleaner environment, two new graffiti removal trucks are essential to
expand these efforts further.

These state-of-the-art vehicles are designed explicitly for graffiti abatement, significantly
improving efficiency and safety for the City’s Community Preservation Program. The
City’s Fleet and Graffiti teams collaborated with Roadline to develop a water recovery
system that prevents environmental contamination from pressure washing water runoff,
ensuring compliance with governmental storm drain regulations. These vehicles and
their unique system provide an economical and effective treatment solution, reducing
disposal costs, guaranteeing results, and improving response times.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Requisitions No. 250913 with National Auto Fleet, No. 250915 with Inland
Kenworth (US), Inc., No. 250917 with Municipal Maintenance Equipment, & No. 250930
with PB Loader Corporation
April 15, 2025
Page 3

The acquisition of these two new graffiti trucks will replace older repurposed service
trucks, bringing the fleet to five specialized graffiti abatement vehicles—one for each
district. They will further expand the graffiti abatement efforts, enhancing the short—and
long-term sustainability of providing a safe and clean community.

Kenworth T880 Allison Super 10 Dump Truck

With the continued growth of the City’s Community Preservation Program, existing
Street Maintenance heavy equipment will be reallocated to address illegal dumping and
homeless encampment cleanup efforts. Acquiring a new Kenworth dump truck will
backfill the needs of Street Maintenance in their daily operations and offer enhanced
equipment functionality and reliability.

With the City’s continued growth, there has been an increased demand for street
maintenance services, including material hauling, debris removal, and construction
support. Therefore, adding this dump truck is a strategic investment to expand the fleet,
reduce waiting times for equipment availability, and improve operational efficiency and
service delivery.

Petersen Lightning Loader

Illegal dumping presents ongoing environmental and public health challenges for our
community, impacting aesthetics, safety, and overall quality of life. The City currently
owns two lightning loaders, which are primarily used to clean illegal dumping sites and
homeless encampments. These responsibilities will be shifting to the City’s Community
Preservation Program; therefore, acquiring a new Petersen Lightning Loader will backfill
the needs of Street Maintenance.
The lightning loader is designed for rapid and efficient collection of large debris. It will
be used by Street Maintenance in their day-to-day operations for debris removal (e.g.,
trees, concrete, etc.), construction support, and drainage vegetation clearing. It will also
play a crucial role in assisting with illegal dumping and homeless encampment cleanup
efforts, providing essential support to mitigate health hazards, safety concerns, and
negative environmental impacts throughout the City. Therefore, acquiring the new
lightning loader will improve operational efficiency and service delivery, reduce the strain
on existing resources, and promote cleaner and safer public spaces

PB Loader B-5 Asphalt Truck

The City’s current paving machine is almost 25 years old. It is classified by the California
Air Resources Board (CARB) as a Tier 1 diesel engine, which limits its operational hours
and will eventually be phased out of use. The new equipment will provide a completely

self-contained vehicle that is immediately ready for daily use. Additionally, it is an
excellent fit for hot patching street maintenance operations, which is the most effective
technique for repairing potholes and other permanent asphalt rehabilitations. This
equipment will easily support the removal of old asphalt material, create a firm base,
tack the hold edges, add hot asphalt mix, compact the material, and seal the patch for
more durable and longer-lasting repairs.

The City will purchase the new and replacement vehicles using cooperative pricing
through individual Sourcewell contracts with specialized vendors.

$1,274,500; funds for the requisitions and the resulting purchase orders are currently
budgeted in Fleet Maintenance equipment capitalized. Operating and maintenance costs
are projected to be approximately $7,700 annually for each vehicle after the vehicle’s
initial year in service.

  CONTRACT

  This Contract is between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. Box 219, Staples, MN
  56479 (Sourcewell) and 72 Hour LLC, dba National Auto Fleet Group, 490 Auto Center Drive,
  Watsonville, CA 95076 (Supplier).

  Sourcewell is a State of Minnesota local government unit and service cooperative created
  under the laws of the State of Minnesota (Minnesota Statutes Section 123A.21) that offers
  cooperative procurement solutions to government entities. Participation is open to eligible
  federal, state/province, and municipal governmental entities, higher education, K-12 education,
  nonprofit, tribal government, and other public entities located in the United States and Canada.
  Sourcewell issued a public solicitation for Class 4-8 Chassis and Cabs with Related Equipment,
  Accessories, and Services from which Supplier was awarded a contract.

  Supplier desires to contract with Sourcewell to provide equipment, products, or services to
  Sourcewell and the entities that access Sourcewell’s cooperative purchasing contracts
  (Participating Entities).

  1. TERM OF CONTRACT

  A. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Contract is effective upon the date of the final signature below.

  EXPIRATION DATE AND EXTENSION. This Contract expires July 9, 2028, unless it is cancelled
  sooner pursuant to Article 22. This Contract allows up to three additional one-year extensions
  upon the request of Sourcewell and written agreement by Supplier. Sourcewell retains the right
  to consider additional extensions beyond seven years as required under exceptional
  circumstances.

  B. SURVIVAL OF TERMS. Notwithstanding any expiration or termination of this Contract, all
  payment obligations incurred prior to expiration or termination will survive, as will the
  following: Articles 11 through 14 survive the expiration or cancellation of this Contract. All
  other rights will cease upon expiration or termination of this Contract.

  2. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES

  This Contract offers an indefinite quantity of sales, and while substantial volume is anticipated,
  sales and sales volume are not guaranteed.

  B. WARRANTY. Supplier warrants that all Equipment, Products, and Services furnished are free
  from liens and encumbrances, and are free from defects in design, materials, and workmanship.

  and distributors must agree to assist the Participating Entity in reaching a resolution in any

  beyond the expiration of the Supplier’s warranty will be passed on to the Participating Entity.

  C.  DEALERS, DISTRIBUTORS, AND/OR RESELLERS. Upon Contract execution and throughout
  the Contract term, Supplier must provide to Sourcewell a current means to validate or
  authenticate Supplier’s authorized dealers, distributors, or resellers relative to the Equipment,
  Products, and Services offered under this Contract, which will be incorporated into this
  Contract by reference. It is the Supplier’s responsibility to ensure Sourcewell receives the most
  current information.

  3. PRICING

  All Equipment, Products, or Services under this Contract will be priced at or below the price
  stated in Supplier’s Proposal.

  When providing pricing quotes to Participating Entities, all pricing quoted must reflect a
  Participating Entity’s total cost of acquisition. This means that the quoted cost is for delivered
  Equipment, Products, and Services that are operational for their intended purpose, and
  includes all costs to the Participating Entity’s requested delivery location.

  Regardless of the payment method chosen by the Participating Entity, the total cost associated
  with any purchase option of the Equipment, Products, or Services must always be disclosed in
  the pricing quote to the applicable Participating Entity at the time of purchase.

  policies and procedures, and all applicable laws.

  032824-KTC

  Solicitation Number: RFP #032824

  CONTRACT

  This Contract is between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. Box 219, Staples, MN
  56479 (Sourcewell) and Kenworth Truck Company, a Division of PACCAR Inc., 10630 NE 38th
  Place, Kirkland, WA 98033 (Supplier).

  Sourcewell is a State of Minnesota local government unit and service cooperative created
  under the laws of the State of Minnesota (Minnesota Statutes Section 123A.21) that offers
  cooperative procurement solutions to government entities. Participation is open to eligible
  federal, state/province, and municipal governmental entities, higher education, K-12 education,
  nonprofit, tribal government, and other public entities located in the United States and Canada.
  Sourcewell issued a public solicitation for Class 4-8 Chassis and Cabs with Related Equipment,
  Accessories, and Services from which Supplier was awarded a contract.

  Supplier desires to contract with Sourcewell to provide equipment, products, or services to
  Sourcewell and the entities that access Sourcewell’s cooperative purchasing contracts
  (Participating Entities).

  1. TERM OF CONTRACT

  A. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Contract is effective upon the date of the final signature below.

  EXPIRATION DATE AND EXTENSION. This Contract expires July 9, 2028, unless it is cancelled
  sooner pursuant to Article 22. This Contract allows up to three additional one-year extensions
  upon the request of Sourcewell and written agreement by Supplier. Sourcewell retains the right
  to consider additional extensions beyond seven years as required under exceptional
  circumstances.

  B. SURVIVAL OF TERMS. Notwithstanding any expiration or termination of this Contract, all
  payment obligations incurred prior to expiration or termination will survive, as will the
  following: Articles 11 through 14 survive the expiration or cancellation of this Contract. All
  other rights will cease upon expiration or termination of this Contract.

  2. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES

  A. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES. Supplier will provide the Equipment, Products, or
  Services as stated in its Proposal submitted under the Solicitation Number listed above.
  Supplier’s Equipment, Products, or Services Proposal (Proposal) is attached and incorporated
  into this Contract.

  All Equipment and Products provided under this Contract must be new and the current model.
  Supplier may offer close-out or refurbished Equipment or Products if they are clearly indicated
  in Supplier’s product and pricing list. Unless agreed to by the Participating Entities in advance,
  Equipment or Products must be delivered as operational to the Participating Entity’s site.

  This Contract offers an indefinite quantity of sales, and while substantial volume is anticipated,
  sales and sales volume are not guaranteed.

  B. WARRANTY. Supplier warrants that all Equipment, Products, and Services furnished are free
  from liens and encumbrances, and are free from defects in design, materials, and workmanship
  pursuant to the express vehicle warranty and extended warranties provided with all Supplier’s
  vehicles. Supplier does not warrant or accept responsibility or liability for any parts separately
  warrantied, for example, body installations, or engines not manufactured by Supplier (which
  carry a separate manufacturer’s warranty). In addition, Supplier warrants the Equipment,
  Products, and Services are suitable for and will perform in accordance with the ordinary use for
  which they are intended. Supplier’s dealers and distributors must agree to assist the
  Participating Entity in reaching a resolution in any dispute over warranty terms with the
  manufacturer. Any manufacturer’s warranty that that is effective past the expiration of the
  Supplier’s warranty will be passed on to the Participating Entity.

  C.  DEALERS, DISTRIBUTORS, AND/OR RESELLERS. Upon Contract execution and throughout
  the Contract term, Supplier must provide to Sourcewell a current means to validate or
  authenticate Supplier’s authorized dealers, distributors, or resellers relative to the Equipment,
  Products, and Services offered under this Contract, which will be incorporated into this
  Contract by reference. It is the Supplier’s responsibility to ensure Sourcewell receives the most
  current information.

  3. PRICING

  All Equipment, Products, or Services under this Contract will be priced at or below the price
  stated in Supplier’s Proposal.

  When providing pricing quotes to Participating Entities, all pricing quoted must reflect a
  Participating Entity’s total cost of acquisition. This means that the quoted cost is for delivered
  Equipment, Products, and Services that are operational for their intended purpose, and
  includes all costs to the Participating Entity’s requested delivery location.

  Regardless of the payment method chosen by the Participating Entity, the total cost associated
  with any purchase option of the Equipment, Products, or Services must always be disclosed in
  the pricing quote to the applicable Participating Entity at the time of purchase.

  A. SHIPPING AND SHIPPING COSTS. All delivered Equipment and Products must be properly
  packaged. Damaged Equipment and Products may be rejected. If the damage is not readily
  apparent at the time of delivery, Supplier must permit the Equipment and Products to be
  returned within a reasonable time at no cost to Sourcewell or its Participating Entities.
  Participating Entities reserve the right to inspect the Equipment and Products at a reasonable
  time after delivery where circumstances or conditions prevent effective inspection of the
  Equipment and Products at the time of delivery. In the event of the delivery of nonconforming
  Equipment and Products, the Participating Entity will notify the Supplier as soon as possible and
  the Supplier will replace nonconforming Equipment and Products with conforming Equipment
  and Products that are acceptable to the Participating Entity.

  Supplier must arrange for and pay for the return shipment on Equipment and Products that arrive
  in a defective or inoperable condition.

  Sourcewell may declare the Supplier in breach of this Contract if the Supplier intentionally
  delivers substandard or inferior Equipment or Products.

  B. SALES TAX. Each Participating Entity is responsible for supplying the Supplier with valid tax-
  exemption certification(s). When ordering, a Participating Entity must indicate if it is a tax-
  exempt entity.

  C. HOT LIST PRICING. At any time during this Contract, Supplier may offer a specific selection
  of Equipment, Products, or Services at discounts greater than those listed in the Contract.
  When Supplier determines it will offer Hot List Pricing, it must be submitted electronically to
  Sourcewell in a line-item format. Equipment, Products, or Services may be added or removed
  from the Hot List at any time through a Sourcewell Price and Product Change Form as defined
  in Article 4 below.

  Hot List program and pricing may also be used to discount and liquidate close-out and
  discontinued Equipment and Products as long as those close-out and discontinued items are
  clearly identified as such. Current ordering process and administrative fees apply. Hot List
  Pricing must be published and made available to all Participating Entities.

  4. PRODUCT AND PRICING CHANGE REQUESTS

  Supplier may request Equipment, Product, or Service changes, additions, or deletions at any
  time. All requests must be made in writing by submitting a signed Sourcewell Price and Product
  Change Request Form to the assigned Sourcewell Supplier Development Administrator. This

  5. PARTICIPATION, CONTRACT ACCESS, AND PARTICIPATING ENTITY REQUIREMENTS

  A. PARTICIPATION. Sourcewell’s cooperative contracts are available and open to public and
  nonprofit entities across the United States and Canada; such as federal, state/province,
  municipal, K-12 and higher education, tribal government, and other public entities.

  The benefits of this Contract should be available to all Participating Entities that can legally
  access the Equipment, Products, or Services under this Contract. A Participating Entity’s
  authority to access this Contract is determined through its cooperative purchasing, interlocal,
  or joint powers laws. Any entity accessing benefits of this Contract will be considered a Service
  Member of Sourcewell during such time of access. Supplier understands that a Participating
  Entity’s use of this Contract is at the Participating Entity’s sole convenience and Participating
  Entities reserve the right to obtain like Equipment, Products, or Services from any other source.

  Supplier is responsible for familiarizing its sales and service forces with Sourcewell contract use
  eligibility requirements and documentation and will encourage potential participating entities
  to join Sourcewell. Sourcewell reserves the right to add and remove Participating Entities to its
  roster during the term of this Contract.

  B. PUBLIC FACILITIES. Supplier’s employees may be required to perform work at government-
  owned facilities, including schools. Supplier’s employees and agents must conduct themselves
  in a professional manner while on the premises, and in accordance with Participating Entity
  policies and procedures, and all applicable laws.

  A. ORDERS AND PAYMENT. To access the contracted Equipment, Products, or Services under

  may use its own forms, but the purchase order should clearly note the applicable Sourcewell
  contract number. All Participating Entity orders under this Contract must be issued prior to
  expiration or cancellation of this Contract; however, Supplier performance, Participating Entity
  payment obligations, and any applicable warranty periods or other Supplier or Participating
  Entity obligations may extend beyond the term of this Contract.

  Supplier’s acceptable forms of payment are included in its attached Proposal. Participating
  Entities will be solely responsible for payment and Sourcewell will have no liability for any
  unpaid invoice of any Participating Entity.

  B. ADDITIONAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS/PARTICIPATING ADDENDUM. Additional terms and
  conditions to a purchase order, or other required transaction documentation, may be
  negotiated between a Participating Entity and Supplier, such as job or industry-specific
  requirements, legal requirements (e.g., affirmative action or immigration status requirements),
  or specific local policy requirements. Some Participating Entities may require the use of a
  Participating Addendum, the terms of which will be negotiated directly between the
  Participating Entity and the Supplier or its authorized dealers, distributors, or resellers, as
  applicable. Any negotiated additional terms and conditions must never be less favorable to the
  Participating Entity than what is contained in this Contract.

  C. SPECIALIZED SERVICE REQUIREMENTS. In the event that the Participating Entity requires
  service or specialized performance requirements not addressed in this Contract (such as e-
  commerce specifications, specialized delivery requirements, or other specifications and
  requirements), the Participating Entity and the Supplier may enter into a separate, standalone
  agreement, apart from this Contract. Sourcewell, including its agents and employees, will not
  be made a party to a claim for breach of such agreement.

  D. TERMINATION OF ORDERS. Participating Entities may terminate an order, in whole or
  in part, immediately upon notice to Supplier in the event of any of the following events:

  1. The Participating Entity fails to receive funding or appropriation from its governing body
  at levels sufficient to pay for the equipment, products, or services to be purchased; or
  2. Federal, state, or provincial laws or regulations prohibit the purchase or change the
  Participating Entity’s requirements.

  E. GOVERNING LAW AND VENUE. The governing law and venue for any action related to a
  Participating Entity’s order will be determined by the Participating Entity making the purchase.

  7. CUSTOMER SERVICE

  A. PRIMARY ACCOUNT REPRESENTATIVE. Supplier will assign an Account Representative to
  Sourcewell for this Contract and must provide prompt notice to Sourcewell if that person is
  changed. The Account Representative will be responsible for:

  x Maintenance and management of this Contract;
  x Timely response to all Sourcewell and Participating Entity inquiries; and
  x Business reviews to Sourcewell and Participating Entities, if applicable.

  B. BUSINESS REVIEWS. Supplier must perform a minimum of one business review with
  Sourcewell per contract year. The business review will cover sales to Participating Entities,
  pricing and contract terms, administrative fees, sales data reports, performance issues, supply
  issues, customer issues, and any other necessary information.

  8. REPORT ON CONTRACT SALES ACTIVITY AND ADMINISTRATIVE FEE PAYMENT

  A. CONTRACT SALES ACTIVITY REPORT. Each calendar quarter, Supplier must provide a
  contract sales activity report (Report) to the Sourcewell Supplier Development Administrator
  assigned to this Contract. Reports are due no later than 45 days after the end of each calendar
  quarter. A Report must be provided regardless of the number or amount of sales during that
  quarter (i.e., if there are no sales, Supplier must submit a report indicating no sales were
  made).

  CONTRACT

  This Contract is between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. Box 219, Staples, MN
  56479 (Sourcewell) and Petersen Industries, Inc., 4000 S.R. 60 W., Lake Wales, FL 33859
  (Vendor).

  Sourcewell is a State of Minnesota local government agency and service cooperative created
  under the laws of the State of Minnesota (Minnesota Statutes Section 123A.21) that offers
  cooperative procurement solutions to government entities. Participation is open to federal,
  state/province, and municipal governmental entities, higher education, K-12 education,
  nonprofit, tribal government, and other public entities located in the United States and Canada.
  Sourcewell issued a public solicitation for Bulk Solid Waste and Recycling Equipment from
  which Vendor was awarded a contract.

  Vendor desires to contract with Sourcewell to provide equipment, products, or services to
  Sourcewell and the entities that access Sourcewell’s cooperative purchasing contracts
  (Participating Entities).

  1. TERM OF CONTRACT

  A. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Contract is effective upon the date of the final signature below.

  B. EXPIRATION DATE AND EXTENSION. This Contract expires June 2, 2025, unless it is cancelled
  sooner pursuant to Article 22. This Contract may be extended up to one additional one-year
  period upon request of Sourcewell and with written agreement by Vendor.

  C. SURVIVAL OF TERMS. Articles 11 through 14 survive the expiration or cancellation of this
  Contract.

  2. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES

  A. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES. Vendor will provide the Equipment, Products, or
  Services as stated in its Proposal submitted under the Solicitation Number listed above.
  Vendor’s Equipment, Products, or Services Proposal (Proposal) is attached and incorporated
  into this Contract.

  version of this list.

  Participating Entity’s total cost of acquisition. This means that the quoted cost is for delivered
  Equipment, Products, and Services that are operational for their intended purpose, and
  includes all costs to the Participating Entity’s requested delivery location.

  Regardless of the payment method chosen by the Participating Entity, the total cost associated
  with any purchase option of the Equipment, Products, or Services must always be disclosed in
  the pricing quote to the applicable Participating Entity at the time of purchase.

  A. SHIPPING AND SHIPPING COSTS. All delivered Equipment and Products must be properly
  packaged. Damaged Equipment and Products may be rejected. If the damage is not readily
  apparent at the time of delivery, Vendor must permit the Equipment and Products to be

  Participating Entities reserve the right to inspect the Equipment and Products at a reasonable

  5. PARTICIPATION, CONTRACT ACCESS, AND PARTICIPATING ENTITY REQUIREMENTS

  A. PARTICIPATION. Sourcewell’s cooperative contracts are available and open to public and

  access the Equipment, Products, or Services under this Contract. A Participating Entity’s
  authority to access this Contract is determined through its cooperative purchasing, interlocal,
  or joint powers laws. Any entity accessing benefits of this Contract will be considered a Service
  Member of Sourcewell during such time of access. Vendor understands that a Participating
  Entity’s use of this Contract is at the Participating Entity’s sole convenience and Participating
  Entities reserve the right to obtain like Equipment, Products, or Services from any other source.

  eligibility requirements and documentation and will encourage potential participating entities
  to join Sourcewell. Sourcewell reserves the right to add and remove Participating Entities to its
  roster during the term of this Contract.

  B. PUBLIC FACILITIES. Vendor’s employees may be required to perform work at government-
  owned facilities, including schools. Vendor’s employees and agents must conduct themselves in
  a professional manner while on the premises, and in accordance with Participating Entity
  policies and procedures, and all applicable laws.

  6. PARTICIPATING ENTITY USE AND PURCHASING

  A. ORDERS AND PAYMENT. To access the contracted Equipment, Products, or Services under
  this Contract, a Participating Entity must clearly indicate to Vendor that it intends to access this
  Contract; however, order flow and procedure will be developed jointly between Sourcewell and
  Vendor. Typically, a Participating Entity will issue an order directly to Vendor. If a Participating
  Entity issues a purchase order, it may use its own forms, but the purchase order should clearly
  note the applicable Sourcewell contract number. All Participating Entity orders under this
  Contract must be issued prior to expiration of this Contract; however, Vendor performance,
  Participating Entity payment, and any applicable warranty periods or other Vendor or
  Participating Entity obligations may extend beyond the term of this Contract.

  CONTRACT

  This Contract is between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. Box 219, Staples, MN
  56479 (Sourcewell) and PB Loader Corporation, 5778 W. Barstow Ave., Fresno, CA 93722
  (Supplier).

  Sourcewell is a State of Minnesota local government unit and service cooperative created
  under the laws of the State of Minnesota (Minnesota Statutes Section 123A.21) that offers
  cooperative procurement solutions to government entities. Participation is open to eligible
  federal, state/province, and municipal governmental entities, higher education, K-12 education,
  nonprofit, tribal government, and other public entities located in the United States and Canada.
  Sourcewell issued a public solicitation for Roadway Maintenance Equipment from which
  Supplier was awarded a contract.

  Supplier desires to contract with Sourcewell to provide equipment, products, or services to
  Sourcewell and the entities that access Sourcewell’s cooperative purchasing contracts
  (Participating Entities).

  1. TERM OF CONTRACT

  A. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Contract is effective upon the date of the final signature below.

  B. EXPIRATION DATE AND EXTENSION. This Contract expires October 11, 2025, unless it is
  cancelled sooner pursuant to Article 22. This Contract may be extended one additional year
  upon the request of Sourcewell and written agreement by Supplier.

  C. SURVIVAL OF TERMS. Notwithstanding any expiration or termination of this Contract, all
  payment obligations incurred prior to expiration or termination will survive, as will the
  following: Articles 11 through 14 survive the expiration or cancellation of this Contract. All
  other rights will cease upon expiration or termination of this Contract.

  2. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES

  A. EQUIPMENT, PRODUCTS, OR SERVICES. Supplier will provide the Equipment, Products, or
  Services as stated in its Proposal submitted under the Solicitation Number listed above.

  This Contract offers an indefinite quantity of sales, and while substantial volume is anticipated,

  B. WARRANTY. Supplier warrants that all Equipment, Products, and Services furnished are free
  from liens and encumbrances, and are free from defects in design, materials, and workmanship.
  In addition, Supplier warrants the Equipment, Products, and Services are suitable for and will
  perform in accordance with the ordinary use for which they are intended. Supplier’s dealers
  and distributors must agree to assist the Participating Entity in reaching a resolution in any

  21. PROVISIONS FOR NON-UNITED STATES FEDERAL ENTITY PROCUREMENTS UNDER
  UNITED STATES FEDERAL AWARDS OR OTHER AWARDS

  Participating Entities that use United States federal grant or FEMA funds to purchase goods or
  services from this Contract may be subject to additional requirements including the
  procurement standards of the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit
  Requirements for Federal Awards, 2 C.F.R. § 200. Participating Entities may have additional
  requirements based on specific funding source terms or conditions. Within this Article, all
  references to “federal” should be interpreted to mean the United States federal government.
  The following list only applies when a Participating Entity accesses Supplier’s Equipment,
  Products, or Services with United States federal funds.

  A. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY. Except as otherwise provided under 41 C.F.R. § 60, all
  contracts that meet the definition of “federally assisted construction contract” in 41 C.F.R. § 60-
  1.3 must include the equal opportunity clause provided under 41 C.F.R. §60-1.4(b), in
  accordance with Executive Order 11246, “Equal Employment Opportunity” (30 FR 12319,
  12935, 3 C.F.R. §, 1964-1965 Comp., p. 339), as amended by Executive Order 11375, “Amending
  Executive Order 11246 Relating to Equal Employment Opportunity,” and implementing
  regulations at 41 C.F.R. § 60, “Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, Equal
  Employment Opportunity, Department of Labor.” The equal opportunity clause is incorporated
  herein by reference.

  B. DAVIS-BACON ACT, AS AMENDED (40 U.S.C. § 3141-3148). When required by federal
  program legislation, all prime construction contracts in excess of $2,000 awarded by non-
  federal entities must include a provision for compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act (40 U.S.C. §
  3141-3144, and 3146-3148) as supplemented by Department of Labor regulations (29 C.F.R. § 5,
  “Labor Standards Provisions Applicable to Contracts Covering Federally Financed and Assisted
  Construction”). In accordance with the statute, contractors must be required to pay wages to
  laborers and mechanics at a rate not less than the prevailing wages specified in a wage
  determination made by the Secretary of Labor. In addition, contractors must be required to pay
  wages not less than once a week. The non-federal entity must place a copy of the current
  prevailing wage determination issued by the Department of Labor in each solicitation. The
  decision to award a contract or subcontract must be conditioned upon the acceptance of the
  wage determination. The non-federal entity must report all suspected or reported violations to
  the federal awarding agency. The contracts must also include a provision for compliance with
  the Copeland “Anti-Kickback” Act (40 U.S.C. § 3145), as supplemented by Department of Labor
  regulations (29 C.F.R. § 3, “Contractors and Subcontractors on Public Building or Public Work
  Financed in Whole or in Part by Loans or Grants from the United States”). The Act provides that
  each contractor or subrecipient must be prohibited from inducing, by any means, any person
  employed in the construction, completion, or repair of public work, to give up any part of the
  compensation to which he or she is otherwise entitled. The non-federal entity must report
  all suspected or reported violations to the federal awarding agency. Supplier must be in
  compliance with all applicable Davis-Bacon Act provisions.

  C. CONTRACT WORK HOURS AND SAFETY STANDARDS ACT (40 U.S.C. § 3701-3708). Where
  applicable, all contracts awarded by the non-federal entity in excess of $100,000 that involve
  the employment of mechanics or laborers must include a provision for compliance with 40
  U.S.C. §§ 3702 and 3704, as supplemented by Department of Labor regulations (29 C.F.R. § 5).
  Under 40 U.S.C. § 3702 of the Act, each contractor must be required to compute the wages of
  every mechanic and laborer on the basis of a standard work week of 40 hours. Work in excess
  of the standard work week is permissible provided that the worker is compensated at a rate of
  not less than one and a half times the basic rate of pay for all hours worked in excess of 40
  hours in the work week. The requirements of 40 U.S.C. § 3704 are applicable to construction
  work and provide that no laborer or mechanic must be required to work in surroundings or
  under working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous. These requirements
  do not apply to the purchases of supplies or materials or articles ordinarily available on the
  open market, or contracts for transportation or transmission of intelligence. This provision is
  hereby incorporated by reference into this Contract. Supplier certifies that during the term of
  an award for all contracts by Sourcewell resulting from this procurement process, Supplier must
  comply with applicable requirements as referenced above.

  D. RIGHTS TO INVENTIONS MADE UNDER A CONTRACT OR AGREEMENT. If the federal award
  meets the definition of “funding agreement” under 37 C.F.R. § 401.2(a) and the recipient or
  subrecipient wishes to enter into a contract with a small business firm or nonprofit organization
  regarding the substitution of parties, assignment or performance of experimental,
  developmental, or research work under that “funding agreement,” the recipient or subrecipient
  must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 401, “Rights to Inventions Made by Nonprofit
  Organizations and Small Business Firms Under Government Grants, Contracts and Cooperative
  Agreements,” and any implementing regulations issued by the awarding agency. Supplier
  certifies that during the term of an award for all contracts by Sourcewell resulting from this
  procurement process, Supplier must comply with applicable requirements as referenced above.

  E. CLEAN AIR ACT (42 U.S.C. § 7401-7671Q.) AND THE FEDERAL WATER POLLUTION CONTROL
  ACT (33 U.S.C. § 1251-1387). Contracts and subgrants of amounts in excess of $150,000 require
  the non-federal award to agree to comply with all applicable standards, orders or regulations
  issued pursuant to the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. § 7401- 7671q) and the Federal Water Pollution
  Control Act as amended (33 U.S.C. § 1251- 1387). Violations must be reported to the Federal
  awarding agency and the Regional Office of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
  Supplier certifies that during the term of this Contract will comply with applicable requirements
  as referenced above.

RECOMMENDATION

  Terrace Apartments located at 2650 East Avenue Q-12; and,

  the security for the completed public street improvements.

This project, located on 25th Street East and Avenue Q-12, constructed public landscape
improvements along the project frontage of 25th Street East and within a new median.

way. The public improvements have been installed per the approved landscape plan and
inspected and approved by City Public Works and Landscape inspection staff.

Code. This action will accept the public landscape improvements as complete and
initiate the City’s release of applicable securities posted for this project per the City’s
subdivision regulations.

shown in the Site Map, Exhibit B, and have been completed to the City Engineer’s
satisfaction as required in the Subdivision/Development Improvement Agreement

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend the City Council:

Adopt Resolution No. CC 2025-033, approving the Five-Year Public Art Work Plan in
accordance with Chapter 15.01 of the Palmdale Municipal Code.

BACKGROUND

The Palmdale City Council approved Resolution No. CC 2020-084, which adopted the
Public Art Master Plan and instructed staff to work actively on its recommendations.
Following this, the Commission and staff created an annual Public Art Work Plan that
outlines ongoing and upcoming public art projects and sets priorities for resources and
funding. This five-year strategy is updated each year to include City-funded projects,
public/private partnerships, maintenance, and a conservation plan. The City Council
reviews and approves the proposed Public Art Work Plan during the annual budget
adoption process.

DISCUSSION

The Public Art Work Plan outlines the steps for carrying out all municipal public art
projects in the City. This includes details on the artwork’s design, location, budget, and
schedule. The expected balance in the Public Art Fund for fiscal year 2025 is $1,630,341.
Most of these funds were allocated from the General Fund to initiate the program.

The Public Art Commission reviewed the Five-Year Public Art Work Plan draft at the
meeting on January 28, 2025, and the final form was reviewed and discussed at their
